draft.title: Categories of crime
card: Crimes are sorted into categories by what they harm or what they involve. The categories help us study and compare offences.
offences that harm or threaten people, such as assault and murder. Against property: offences involving another's goods, such as theft, break and enter and property damage.
Drug offences involve illegal drugs, such as supplying a prohibited drug. Public order offences disturb public peace or safety, such as offensive behaviour or affray.

White collar crime is non-violent crime, often by people in business or office roles, such as fraud and insider trading. Driving offences involve vehicles, such as drink driving. Offences against the state threaten the government or the nation, such as treason and terrorism.
draft.remember: A crime's category depends on what it harms or involves: people, property, drugs, public peace, business trust, roads or the state.

a.q: Which offence is an offence against the person?
a.why: Assault harms or threatens another person, so it is an offence against the person. Affray is tempting because it involves violence, but it is a public order offence because it disturbs public safety.
a.clue: Which offence directly harms or threatens a individual?

b.q: Dev is an accountant in Newcastle. He secretly moves client money into his own account and hides it in the records. Which category best fits his offence?
b.why: Dev is a non-violent offender who misused his office role and his clients' trust, which is white collar crime. Offences against the person is tempting because clients lose out, but nobody was harmed or threatened physically.
b.clue: No one was hurt, and his job gave him the chance.
